source: NCERT Class X, Understanding Economic Development, Economics Ch. 5.

sections.heading: 1. Why Consumer Protection?
points: Consumers face **exploitation** in the market: **underweight/measure, adulteration, high prices, false information, defective goods, poor after-sale service**.
Sellers often have **more power/information** than individual buyers; large companies with money and reach can mislead consumers.
Hence the **consumer movement** arose to protect buyers' interests, forcing rules and standards on business.

sections.heading: 2. The Consumer Movement and COPRA
points: The **consumer movement** in India grew due to dissatisfaction with unfair trade practices; it began as social force in the 1960s and grew stronger in the 1970s–80s.
The **Consumer Protection Act, 1986 (COPRA)** was a major step — it set up a **three-tier quasi-judicial machinery** for redressal.
**24 December** is celebrated as **National Consumers' Day** (COPRA enacted).

points.text: COPRA guarantees consumers the following rights:
sub: **Right to Safety** — protection against goods/services hazardous to life and health.
**Right to be Informed** — details of price, quantity, ingredients, expiry, etc.
**Right to Choose** — access to a variety of goods at competitive prices.
**Right to Seek Redressal** — compensation against unfair trade/exploitation.
**Right to Represent / be Heard** — form consumer organisations.

sections.heading: 4. Standards, Redressal and Duties
points: **Logos and certification marks** assure quality: **ISI** (industrial goods/electrical), **Agmark** (agricultural products), **Hallmark** (gold jewellery).
**Three-tier redressal** under COPRA: **District (up to a limit), State, and National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission** — consumers can appeal upward.
Consumers should demand a **cash memo/bill and warranty**, check standard marks, and be aware of their rights.
Note: The **Consumer Protection Act, 2019** replaced COPRA 1986 (adds e-commerce, central consumer protection authority) — but NCERT text focuses on COPRA 1986.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: COPRA = Consumer Protection Act, 1986; National Consumers' Day = 24 December.
Rights: Safety, Information, Choice, Redressal, Representation.
ISI = industrial goods; Agmark = agricultural products; Hallmark = gold.
Three-tier redressal: District, State, National commissions.
Consumer Protection Act 2019 replaced COPRA 1986 (e-commerce, CCPA).

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **COPRA was enacted in 1986**; National Consumers' Day = **24 December**.
The redressal machinery is **three-tier** (District → State → National).
The **Right to be Informed** covers price, quantity, ingredients and expiry.
